name: Longest rota with no repeat
brief:
A support team's rota lists who is on call each day. Management wants the longest run of consecutive days in which nobody was on call twice.

Write `longest_without_repeat(rota)`, which returns the length of that run, or 0 for an empty rota.

Example. For `rota = ['ana', 'ben', 'cat', 'ana', 'dev', 'ben', 'ana']` the days `cat, ana, dev, ben` have no repeat. Every run of five repeats someone, so the answer is 4.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 200{,}000$ days, names strings or whole numbers.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Growing a set from every start day is too slow.
Each test has its own 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Keep a dict from each name to the last day it appeared. When today's name was last seen inside the window, move the window's left edge to the day after.

examples.note: cat, ana, dev and ben are four different people in a row.
Two days running by the same person, so the best run is one day.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: The window is every day since the last repeat, so only the left edge needs care.
A name seen before the left edge is no repeat: check `last[name] >= left`, or the edge jumps backwards.
Each day is one dict look-up, so the work is $O(n)$.
